source.title: Is Random Attention Sufficient for Sequence Modeling? Disentangling Trainable Components in the Transformer
source.authors: Yihe Dong; Lorenzo Noci; M. Khodak; Mufan Li

page_placements.theme: Induction-like attention from random or frozen query-key weights

record.tranche_reason: It tests induction-head behavior using task accuracy and an attention-pattern visualization in trained Transformer variants, rather than reproducing the original training-dynamics analysis.
record.gate_note: The paper reports induction-task accuracy and describes a Frozen-QK induction circuit. It does not measure when heads form during training, loss bumps, or loss changes with token index. Language-model perplexity is not an in-context-learning-by-token-index measure. Other cited findings are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study gives a new-setting result on whether induction heads form. A 2-layer Llama-style Transformer with query and key weights frozen at initialization is shown (Figure 3) to form a previous-token head in layer 0 and an induction head in layer 1. The evidence is one qualitative visualization; task accuracies are capability measures, not head measurements.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that trainable query and key weights are not required to form induction heads or other specialized circuits. Frozen-QK solves the retrieval and k-hop tasks and nearly matches standard perplexity. MixiT, with input-independent attention, cannot form such circuits, which hurts it on induction tasks and language modelling. They read this as a built-in inductive bias of the Transformer toward forming circuits.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains Llama-based variants with frozen or fixed components and evaluates synthetic retrieval and k-hop tasks, including a qualitative attention-pattern visualization; it does not reproduce the original training-dynamics analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Induction-task performance differs by architecture: Frozen-QK performs near the standard model, while MixiT with fixed input-independent attention performs poorly.

fits_no_version.finding: Fixing the attention to an input-independent random matrix (MixiT) collapses accuracy on induction-requiring tasks: k-hop 48.58%, retrieval 11.24%. Algorithmic and memorization tasks stay near standard levels. On retrieval, Frozen-QK degrades faster than the standard model as the number of pairs grows (Figure 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction-requiring tasks need input-dependent attention, but not trainable query and key weights.

record.problems: The induction-head mechanism is illustrated qualitatively for a retrieval example, with no numeric head-strength measure or uncertainty estimates. The k-hop test set contains 100 samples. The paper does not measure training-time formation or token-index in-context learning.

untested.parts: No attention-only models are trained. The two-head composition is shown only qualitatively in a model with MLPs, with no composition scores or ablations.
Formation timing, abrupt onset, in-context-learning gain and the loss bump are not measured.
No loss-by-token-index measure and no attribution of in-context learning to induction heads in large models.
Only Llama-style variants trained on synthetic retrieval are examined. Heads are not inspected in the language-modelling models or across sizes, seeds or modalities.
The training data and setup are not varied in order to study induction-head formation.
Few-shot task learning is not separated from copying.

record.verdict_notes: The head-level evidence is one visualized retrieval example with no quantitative head scores, so the V4 support is weak. Task accuracies were relinked to 'none' because they measure capability, not induction-head presence. The MixiT failures should not count against V4, because that architecture cannot express content-based attention by design. V1 was not credited: the models include MLPs, and the circuit is not quantified.

versions.untested_parts: The tested models are Llama-based decoder Transformers with MLPs, not attention-only Transformers; the paper does not track the circuit's formation during training.
No training-time onset, narrow formation window, in-context-learning gain, or training-loss bump is measured.
No test measures how much loss falls with token index in large Transformers or whether induction heads account for most such in-context learning.
The paper compares Llama-based architectural variants, but does not test multiple model families, modalities, or independent training runs, nor a systematic sweep over sizes.
The paper does not vary data or training setup to measure how they affect induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
It does not separate few-shot task learning from repeated-token copying or test which mechanisms mainly carry few-shot learning.
It does not examine formation trajectories or determine whether formation consists of multiple transitions.

rows.subject: Standard
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated accuracy on the k-hop induction-head task
rows.note: The paper describes this task as requiring induction heads.
rows.check: Standard-model k-hop accuracy is a capability score. No heads were inspected, so it does not show induction heads arising. It is a comparator, not evidence on a version.

rows.subject: Standard
rows.note: The paper says Transformer models typically solve retrieval by forming induction heads.
rows.check: Standard-model retrieval accuracy. The induction-head link is the authors' citation of prior work, not a measurement in this paper.

rows.subject: Frozen-MLP
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated accuracy on the k-hop induction-head task
rows.note: The paper attributes this strong performance to Frozen-MLP's trainable attention modules.
rows.check: Frozen-MLP k-hop accuracy is a capability score with no head-level measurement.

rows.subject: Frozen-MLP
rows.note: The paper says the trainable attention modules perform to almost perfect accuracy.
rows.check: Frozen-MLP retrieval accuracy is a capability score with no head-level measurement.

rows.subject: Frozen-QK
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated accuracy on the k-hop induction-head task
rows.note: The authors characterize Frozen-QK as solving the task on par with the standard Transformer.
rows.check: Frozen-QK k-hop accuracy (96.73% vs 99.99%) is a capability score. The authors infer induction heads from it, but no heads are shown for the 5-layer k-hop model.

rows.check: Frozen-QK retrieval accuracy (97.01%) is a capability score. The head evidence for this model is in Figure 3 (r9), not in this accuracy.

rows.subject: MixiT
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated accuracy on the k-hop induction-head task
rows.note: The authors state that MixiT is unable to solve the induction task because it cannot form specialized circuits.
rows.check: MixiT's attention is fixed and input-independent by construction, so it cannot implement content-based induction. Its low accuracy (48.58%) is an architectural impossibility, not evidence that induction heads fail to appear in transformers. Its state should not be 'absent' against V4.

source_check.locator_found: Table 1: MixiT k-hop 48.58%, Standard 99.99%; Section 2 specifies input-independent frozen mixing; Appendix C.1 supplies task conditions.

rows.subject: MixiT
rows.note: The authors state that MixiT is unable to solve the retrieval task because it cannot form specialized circuits.
rows.check: Same as r7: MixiT retrieval accuracy of 11.24% reflects an architecture that cannot express induction attention. No heads were measured.

rows.subject: Frozen-QK
rows.operation_detail: Visualized attention patterns in the retrieval task
rows.measure: Qualitative induction-head pattern: the first head attends to the previous token, and the second-layer head retrieves the correct token
rows.note: The paper identifies the visualization as an induction head in Frozen-QK; it does not provide a numeric measure of the pattern.
rows.check: This is the only head-level evidence: one qualitative example, with no numeric prefix-matching or copying score. The model has MLPs, so it is not the attention-only setting V1 names; linked to V4 only.
